title: Building a strong knowledge-sharing strategy for the plant floor
summary: Learn to build a knowledge-sharing strategy that captures expert knowledge and delivers it to plant floor workers through AI, AR systems and a reliable network.
body_markdown:
These repositories often look like digital maintenance knowledge bases integrated with a CMMS, or asset-specific libraries within a[connected-worker platform](https://www.belden.com/blog/Supporting-Remote-Connected-Workers-Who-Keep-Plants-Running) ; they **tie documents, media, records and expertise to assets and tasks** . People responsible for assets, shifts and production lines can all use this system to contribute insights. To make the information usable, every entry should be organized around the equipment, task, operating condition or issue it relates to.


The repository should be treated as a living operational resource: Employees can contribute to it as they learn new techniques or encounter unexpected exceptions, and original inputs can be validated and updated as procedures and assets change.


### Documentation becomes real-time guidance with AI and AR systems


Once a repository is in place, **agentic AI can connect documented expertise to the people who need it** , whenever they’re ready to use it.


A new technician doesn’t have to spend precious time looking through paper manuals or searching for the single coworker who might remember how to recalibrate a piece of equipment that’s rarely serviced. Instead, based on the task and asset in question, AI can find relevant information, provide equipment history and context, and walk the user through the steps to complete the work.


This guidance can be delivered through a tablet or laptop, or it can be presented in a hands-free format that supports the flow of physical labor: A technician can use an AR system as they work through an unfamiliar issue. For example, as they inspect a conveyor motor, they could wear an AR headset that provides step-by-step guidance within their field of view. It could display information about torque specs and which bolts to check, without the technician setting down their tools or searching for a manual. *(It’s important to note that workers should always stay alert and be aware of their surroundings, especially when they work near moving parts, energized equipment or other hazards. They should never rely on an AR system in place of standard lockout/tagout or other safety procedures.)*


While this isn’t a replacement for training—and it’s not a replacement for people, either—it can **help new workers onboard faster and give them confidence to troubleshoot independently** . And in an industry where skilled labor is hard to find and keep, this capability can make technical roles appealing to a workforce more accustomed to interacting with digital tools.


## Preparing your network for real-time access


If you plan to give a new engineer access to an AR system or put a tablet in the hands of a novice operator, know that these devices offer no value if they can’t reliably access information from the knowledge repository.
